subject: MSA / Order Form — Indemnity redlines and next steps (Lark Systems)
messages:
From: Emily Park <emily@larksystems.com>
To: jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com
Cc: procurement@larksystems.com
Date: 2027-03-12T08:14:00-07:00
Subject: MSA / Order Form — Indemnity redlines

Jonas,

Thanks for the draft MSA and order form — appreciate the quick turnaround. Our procurement and legal teams flagged the indemnity section as a blocker for procurement sign-off. Main points from our side: a) Lark needs the right to control the defense for third-party IP claims that arise from our use of the service; b) we need clarity on whether "generated output" is within Redwood's indemnity scope; and c) evidence/forensics timelines — we need a guaranteed SLA for access to logs/evidence (48 hours preferred).

Attached are our redlines (attachment: Lark_MS_A_redlines.pdf). Can you confirm whether Redwood is willing to: 1) accept control-of-defense for 3P IP claims; 2) agree to a carveout for model-generated content (or alternatively limit Redwood's indemnity to direct code/model IP); and 3) commit to the evidence access window?

We'd like to move quickly — procurement hopes to close within two weeks if we can resolve indemnity.

Thanks,
Emily Park
Head of Procurement, Lark Systems
[Attachment: Lark_MS_A_redlines.pdf (pdf)]

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
To: Emily Park <emily@larksystems.com>
Cc: kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com, ben.carter@redwoodinference.com, grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2027-03-13T10:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MSA / Order Form — Indemnity redlines

Emily — thanks and got the redlines. Looping in legal and sales to propose a pragmatic path. High-level proposal from Redwood to address your three points: 

- Control of defense: Redwood is ok with Lark controlling the defense for third-party IP claims that solely concern Lark's own product integrations, provided Redwood has the right to participate and approve counsel (standard carve-ins). For claims that relate to our model weights/underlying code, Redwood needs control.
- Model-generated output: propose a narrow carveout — Redwood will defend/reimburse for third-party claims alleging infringement of pre-existing model code or packaged model weights, but we cannot accept broad liability for customer-created prompts or customer-supplied content.
- Evidence & access SLA: we can commit to a 72-hour evidence access SLA for logs and KV cache snapshots for claims that meet the indemnity notice threshold; shorter windows create operational risk for other customers.

Kimberly — can you convert the above into a redline candidate? Ben — want your take on whether we can accept a 72-hour SLA from a sales/ops standpoint. Emily — if the compromise above looks directionally ok, we can run a one-hour call Wed to finalize.

Cheers,
Jonas
VP, Commercial Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
To: jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com, emily@larksystems.com
Cc: ben.carter@redwoodinference.com, grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2027-03-13T14:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MSA / Order Form — Indemnity redlines (draft counter)

Emily / Jonas — drafting thoughts attached (redwood-counter-20270313.docx). Key legal tradeoffs and suggested language: 

1) Right to control defense: offer a split approach — Lark may control defense for claims arising solely from Lark's configuration, integration, or customer data, subject to Redwood's right to replace counsel if Redwood reasonably determines a conflict of interest. For claims that implicate Redwood's models, infrastructure, or pre-trained components, Redwood will retain control. 

2) Model output carveout: propose an explicit definition of "Model Output Claims" (claims alleging IP in text/code produced by the model). Redwood accepts indemnity for claims that allege infringement of third-party code incorporated into our distributed model artifacts (e.g., prepackaged weights). Redwood will not accept indemnity for creative output claims where the only allegation is that the model produced content similar to public material — those are governed by the limited-output liability framework.

3) Evidence & cooperation: require prompt notice (30 days after claim), Redwood to provide logs and relevant KV cache snapshots within 72 hours of a valid request, and Lark to preserve evidence and provide a single technical point of contact. Add a narrow confidentiality carve to enable evidence-sharing with vendor redaction.

4) Remedies and limits: propose defend-and-reimburse with an overall liability cap tied to the order form value (e.g., 12 months of fees) and insurance-offset mechanics. Also include a mutual obligation to escalate to execs if a claim would materially exceed the cap. 

This wording keeps risk contained while giving Lark meaningful protections. If Lark insists on full control of defense for all IP claims we should push for an insurance offset and a higher cap.

Attached: redwood-counter-20270313.docx (proposed redline).

-Kim
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood-counter-20270313.docx (docx)]

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com, jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com
Cc: emily@larksystems.com, grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2027-03-16T09:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MSA / Order Form — Indemnity redlines

Quick operational note from sales/CS perspective: 72 hours for evidence access is workable but ops needs clarity on the scope of "logs" (we should limit to tenant-scoped requestables: request metadata, request/response payloads for the session id(s) provided, and KV cache snapshots for affected requests). Anything requiring a multi-tenant forensic pull will need a formal SRE window.

Also - if we agree to defend/reimburse split, recommend we set the cap to 12 months of committed fees for the order form and commit to assisting with sourcing insurance if Lark needs higher limits. This keeps procurement moving and avoids enterprise counsel stalls. If Lark wants full right-to-defend we should ask for insurance and a somewhat higher cap.

Two asks for Kim/Jonas: 1) confirm the exact artifact list Redwood will produce under the 72-hour SLA; 2) confirm a fallback timeline (e.g., SRE can do a deeper pull within 7 business days on prioritized incidents).

Thanks — happy to take this on the Wed call.

- Ben
Director, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Rachel Green <rachel.green@bakerlaw.com>
To: kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com, emily@larksystems.com
Cc: jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com, ben.carter@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2027-03-17T11:00:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MSA / Order Form — Indemnity redlines (Lark Systems position)

Kim / Emily — quick response from Lark's counsel. Lark's procurement stance is that control of the defense is critical because: a) early litigation strategy can materially change preservation obligations; and b) Lark does not want Redwood's commercial interests (multi-tenant continuity) to limit Lark's ability to pursue remedies. That said, Lark is open to a compromise where Redwood can step in to lead the defense where Redwood's pre-existing IP is the clear subject, or where Redwood assumes fees under an agreed insurance-offset mechanism.

On model-output claims: Lark still pushes for coverage if the output incorporates or reproduces a third party's copyrighted code/text, provided Lark can show a plausible nexus to Redwood's model artifacts (e.g., output includes a verbatim block present in a known dataset). If Redwood will limit its exposure by requiring a threshold of technical evidence (e.g., matched-hash or provenance), Lark can accept narrower standards.

Finally, Lark will accept a 72-hour artifact SLA if Redwood commits to a single point-of-contact in engineering and a written handoff procedure for forensic pulls.

We can take the compromise language in Kim's doc as a good starting point but will need to preserve the right to control defense in the final MSA.

-Rachel Green
BakerLaw LLP (counsel to Lark Systems)

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
To: Emily Park <emily@larksystems.com>
Cc: kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com, ben.carter@redwoodinference.com, grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com, rachel.green@bakerlaw.com
Date: 2027-03-18T16:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MSA / Order Form — Indemnity redlines and next steps

Thanks everyone — helpful thread. Short summary and proposed next steps: 

1) Agreement-in-principle: parties converge on a split-control approach (Lark controls defense for claims tied solely to Lark's integrations/data; Redwood controls defense for claims tied to our pre-trained model artifacts), with a formal mechanism for Redwood to step in where there is overlap.
2) Evidence SLA: Redwood to provide tenant-scoped logs, request/response payloads and KV cache snapshots within 72 hours; SRE deep-dive within 7 business days if required. Redwood will publish a short forensic handoff runbook and a named engineering point of contact.
3) Remedies & cap: propose cap = 12 months of order-form fees plus standard insurance offset. If Lark needs higher limits to close, we can discuss a scoped insurance rider (sales to fast-track).
4) Next steps: Kim will circulate a redline that adopts the split-control language and the 72-hour artifact list by end of day tomorrow. Emily / Rachel please flag any language that would preserve Lark's practical ability to control defense (we are specifically trying to avoid duplicative counsel/schedule fights).

Jonas to schedule a 60-minute call for Thu 10:00am PT — link and agenda in HubSpot. If we can get mutual agreement on the redline in that call, procurement aims to sign the order form within 48 hours after call.
